content: Nicotine nasal spray is prescribed to assist individuals in quitting smoking. It is intended to be used in conjunction with a comprehensive smoking cessation program, which may include support groups, counseling, or specific behavioral modification techniques. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as smoking cessation aids. It works by delivering nicotine to the body to alleviate withdrawal symptoms associated with smoking cessation and to reduce the urge to smoke. Nicotine nasal spray is available as a liquid that is sprayed into the nostrils. You should carefully follow the instructions on your prescription label and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the spray exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or use it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Your doctor will likely recommend starting with one or two doses per hour. Each dose consists of two sprays, one in each nostril. You should not exceed five doses per hour or 40 doses per day (24 hours). After eight weeks of use, once your body has adjusted to not smoking, your doctor may gradually reduce your dose over the next four to six weeks until you are no longer using the spray. Follow your doctor’s instructions for tapering your nicotine dose. Nicotine nasal spray has the potential to be habit-forming. Do not use a larger dose, use it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed. To use the nasal spray, follow these steps: 1. Wash your hands. 2. Gently blow your nose to clear your nasal passages. 3. Remove the cap of the nasal spray by pressing in the circles on the side of the bottle. 4. Prime the pump before the first use by holding the bottle in front of a tissue or paper towel and pumping the spray bottle six to eight times until a fine mist appears. Discard the tissue or towel. 5. Tilt your head back slightly. 6. Insert the tip of the bottle as far as comfortably possible into one nostril, pointing the tip toward the back of your nose. 7. Breathe through your mouth. 8. Pump the spray firmly and quickly one time. Do not sniff, swallow, or inhale while spraying. 9. If your nose runs, gently sniff to keep the spray in your nose. Wait two to three minutes before blowing your nose. 10. Repeat steps 6–8 for the second nostril. 11. Replace the cover on the spray bottle. 12. If you have not used the spray for 24 hours, prime the pump one or two times into a tissue. Avoid over-priming, as this will reduce the amount of medication in the container. If you have not stopped smoking after four weeks of use, consult your doctor. They can help you understand why you were unable to quit and develop a plan to try again. You can also ask your pharmacist or doctor for a copy of the manufacturer’s patient information. This medication may be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before using nicotine nasal spray, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to nicotine or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Be sure to mention medications such as acetaminophen, alpha-blockers, beta-blockers, caffeine-containing medications, cough and cold medications, imipramine, insulin, isoproterenol, oxazepam, pentazocine, and theophylline. Your doctor may need to adjust the doses of your medications once you stop smoking. Inform your doctor if you have recently had a heart attack or if you have a history of nasal problems (e.g., allergies, sinus issues, or polyps), asthma, heart disease, angina, irregular heartbeat, circulation problems (e.g., Buerger’s disease or Raynaud’s phenomenon), hyperthyroidism, pheochromocytoma, insulin-dependent diabetes, ulcers, high blood pressure, or kidney or liver disease. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using nicotine nasal spray, contact your doctor immediately, as nicotine may harm the fetus. It is essential to stop smoking completely while using nicotine nasal spray. Continuing to smoke while using the spray may result in side effects. Be aware that you may still experience some withdrawal symptoms, such as dizziness, anxiety, sleep disturbances, depression, fatigue, and muscle pain. If these symptoms occur, consult your doctor about adjusting your nicotine dose. You may also experience side effects when first using the spray, such as throat irritation, sneezing, coughing, watery eyes, or a runny nose. Wait five minutes after using the spray before driving or operating machinery. Discuss the safe use of caffeinated beverages with your doctor while using this medication. Nicotine nasal spray may cause mild side effects, including a hot, peppery sensation in the back of the nose or throat, runny nose, throat irritation, watery eyes, sneezing, or coughing. Inform your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Serious side effects, such as a rapid heart rate, require immediate medical attention. Contact your doctor if you experience any unusual problems while using this medication. Store nicotine nasal spray bottles, both used and unused, out of reach of children and pets. Keep the bottles at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of used spray bottles with the child-resistant cover in place. Discard any outdated or no longer needed medication. Consult your pharmacist about proper disposal methods. In case of accidental ingestion of nicotine nasal spray, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include paleness, cold sweat, nausea, drooling, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, fainting, hearing or vision problems, uncontrollable shaking, confusion, weakness, or seizures. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Handle nicotine nasal spray carefully, as the bottle may break if dropped. If a spill occurs, wear rubber gloves and clean the area immediately with a cloth or paper towel. Avoid touching the liquid. Dispose of the used cloth or towel in the trash. Carefully pick up broken glass with a broom and wash the spill area multiple times. If the nicotine solution comes into contact with your skin, lips, mouth, eyes, or ears, rinse the affected area immediately with plain water. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
